headline: High: shared broad network egress and MCP/browser surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection risk is moderate via shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API surfaces; next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language commands. That creates a plausible path where Firecrawl-sourced content is fed into next-ai-draw-io as instructions or prompts. No shared filesystem is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP messages without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF next-ai-draw-io treats imported text or diagrams as trusted instructions, malicious content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Sanitize Firecrawl output before passing it to next-ai-draw-io.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from scraped content.
Disable MCP routes for untrusted content paths.
Review any natural-language command parsing for prompt-injection markers.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and handle sensitive classes: Firecrawl touches API keys, screenshots, and structured data; next-ai-draw-io handles files and can call multiple third-party model APIs. If they share a workspace or pass raw content, sensitive data can leave the environment through next-ai-draw-io's external model calls. The lack of documented isolation warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF Firecrawl outputs API keys, screenshots, or structured data into files consumed by next-ai-draw-io, leakage can occur.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those files to OpenAI/Anthropic/Vertex/OpenRouter or similar APIs, the data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs in a separate, access-controlled directory.
Block sensitive fields before handing files to next-ai-draw-io.
Use local-only models for sensitive documents.
Turn off automatic upload of file contents to external APIs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and next-ai-draw-io can use MCP while Firecrawl exposes API/CLI surfaces. If they operate on the same mutable workspace or shared credentials, concurrent writes or conflicting API actions are plausible. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same files or diagrams concurrently, edits can overwrite each other.
IF both agents mutate shared API-backed resources without locks, race conditions can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes to shared files.
Use file locks around diagram or export steps.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data; next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and can render or act on imported content. If next-ai-draw-io treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, a bad scrape or hallucinated extraction can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. The interaction is plausible in default workflows, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as source-of-truth for diagram generation, errors propagate into the final artifact.
IF next-ai-draw-io auto-applies extracted facts without verification, incorrect content becomes user-visible output.
mitigations: Require human review before diagram generation.
Cross-check scraped facts against a second source.
Mark Firecrawl outputs as untrusted input.
Disable auto-apply for extracted entities.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before rendering or export.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl explicitly handles API keys and web content, while next-ai-draw-io handles documents and can send them to multiple third-party model providers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and residency if regulated or sensitive documents are processed through external APIs. The profiles do not document a specific residency breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are routed from Firecrawl into next-ai-draw-io's external model APIs, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF the operator requires local-only processing but enables cloud providers in next-ai-draw-io, compliance gaps appear.
mitigations: Route regulated data only to local models.
Redact secrets before export.
Document which provider processes each document class.
Disable cloud providers for sensitive projects.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class.
